searchText: consensus layer call in 17 minutes call now Quick call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/HyjI-xy8K Re: The Merge naming in today’s call There are some previous discussions here: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/ethereum-roadmapping-improvements/6653/14 Betelgeuse. I mean, is there even any contention? long, hard-to-spell name that devs have to type a million times B star names Baham Baten Kaitos Becrux Beid BELLATRIX BETELGEUSE Botein Brachium more here https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_proper_names_of_stars but yeah, I do think Betelgeuse is the coolest. Bellatrix is pretty badass too. Can't find a link in any of those names or stellar structures to the merge... will keep digging I maintain that ""V1309 Scorpii" is a no brainer, even more given that my brand of spanish does not distinguish "V" from "B" 🙂 Brachium is a binary. Not a massive fan of the name, though. Perhaps someone can come with a city named after a body part like leg or arm, since Betelgeuse means "man with an amputated leg/arm" in different cultures. Or we could stop trying to be clever about it, pick whichever star name we like best, and move on. But there's the EL side as well, and synchronicity would be good Good product delivery is an issue :) Ooh, this might be the perfect place for my favorite group decision making approach: 1. Pick someone from "the group" at random 2. That person picks whomever they wish to be the one who makes the decision. I literally use that system for my weekly seminar. But then everyone is on the same footing. Here I foresee a battle to decide who belongs in that group with many people resigning from the EF :) where's that picture from <@301186049323958275> that describes governance 😂 Yeah, our ill-defined "group" makes it hard to apply fun mechanics like this. EL hard forks are devcon locations, CL hard forks are star names. I don't see any reason for this to change, and we aren't going to have synchronized hard forks anyway (at least this time around). Seems to me that we're over-complicating the whole thing. The merge is an event that happens after both layers have been upgraded, and that's what most non-devs will care about. The hard forks are just pieces of infrastructure that are being upgraded to allow the merge to take place, so not sure that attempting to add significance to their names is a worthwhile effort. Oh no need to argue, I'm sure most will agree (including me) that any name, or even no name, is fine, as long as it happens
